messages:
Claire (AM): opening PotentialBank POC thread. They want Redwood Private in their AWS account, a single stable egress IP for allowlisting, and an answer on whether client source IP can be preserved. POC window: 7 business days.
Tom (SE): quick clarifiers: do they require client IP to show up in logs of downstream services, or just in our app logs? Also, will corporate TLS inspection sit in the egress path?
Claire (AM): downstream services need original client IP (for auditing). They also said corp TLS inspection is likely.
Luis (NetOps): options:
- PrivateLink for control-plane connectivity (interface endpoints) is the lowest friction cross-account. It gives stable DNS names and avoids peering/route table changes.
- To preserve client IP to downstream you must run the serving plane in the customer's VPC behind an NLB with proxy-protocol v2. NAT Gateways will SNAT (lose client IP).
Tom (SE): short config snippet customers can run to validate PrivateLink: 
```
curl -v https://vpce-0f1e2d3c.vpce-svc-abc.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: api.redwood-inference.com'
```
Luis (NetOps): egress allowlist patterns we recommend: prefer FQDN allowlist (*.redwood-inference.com and model-registry.redwood-inference.com). If they require IPs, have them provision NAT Gateway(s) with EIPs per AZ and supply those EIPs to security.
Maya (InfoSec): questionnaire wording to paste: "No public inbound ports required. Outbound only: HTTPS (443) to control-plane FQDNs (*.redwood-inference.com) and model store endpoints (s3.amazonaws.com or model-registry FQDN). TLS 1.2+ enforced. For stable egress allowlist provide NAT EIP(s) or use interface endpoints. Customer-managed KMS supported for Private deployments; KMS usage is audit-logged in CloudTrail."
Tom (SE): cost/ops note for sales: two POC patterns to present to the customer: 1) Minimal: reuse existing NAT/egress (low infra cost) but lose client IP. 2) Preserve-IP: deploy NLBs + proxy-protocol OR run fully in-customer with dedicated NAT Gateways + EIPs (higher infra cost). Include ballpark NAT Gateway/EIP charges in the quote.
Claire (AM): action items: 1) Tom: post one-page diagram + example curl (today). 2) Luis: short firewall + NAT/EIP runbook (EOD). 3) Maya: final questionnaire snippet + links to SOC2/ISO (tomorrow). 4) Sales: include two pricing patterns in POC quote.
infra-bot: sandbox for PotentialBank POC provisioned in us-west-2 (build-211). :rocket:
Claire (AM): thanks all 44d will brief customer tomorrow and attach diagram.
